lines.text: Anis stares intently at her desk.
Every inch is scrawled with scribbles, so crude she can barely bring herself to read them.
She grabs a wet wipe from her bag and tries to clean them, but they won't budge.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: ... Permanent marker, huh?
Anis scans the classroom.
There's chatter here, soft snores there, music spilling from headphones, pages turning.
And through it all, she knows that they're all watching her.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Who the heck did this?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Huh?!
She gets no reaction at all, as though she's not in the room.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Oi! Who the hell did this?!
Still no reaction.
Anis strides up to a girl talking with her friends.
The girl desperately tries to ignore her, but Anis leans in, their faces just inches apart.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Hey, sorry to cut in, but do you know who messed with my desk?
"I-I don't know," comes the predictable reply. Meanwhile, Anis stares at her without blinking.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Was it you?
Watching the girl vehemently deny it, Anis furrows her brows in frustration.
as she straightens and shouts at the class.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I don't even care who did this, just tell me why!

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Huh!? What the hell?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: If you're gonna screw with me, the least you can do is give me a reason!
The classroom becomes so quiet that you can hear a pin drop.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: ... Tch. Seriously, this is driving me nuts.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: And it's not even the first time.
Anis sits at her desk and pulls out another wet wipe.
She scrubs furiously, and the scribbles start to come off, little by little.
The red writing comes off far more easily than the rest.
She stares at the red stains left on the wipe, then she shoots to her feet.
Without warning, she clamps a hand around the back of the girl's neck in the front row.

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: Argh...!

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Hey, class prez! You're supposed to set the example, so care to explain why you pulled a stunt like that? And don't act like it's your first time, either.

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: I-it wasn't me!

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Weren't you bragging about that new lipstick just the other day?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: The color's hard to miss.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Thought you said it was expensive, but here you are using it to scribble. Must be nice having money to burn.
Anis clamps down harder on the nape of the girl's neck.

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: I-I wasn't the only one!

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: But you're in on this too! C'mon, class prez, step up and take the hit for the whole class!

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: Eeeeeek...!
The class president rips herself away from Anis's grip, rubbing her neck as she glares icily.

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: You wanna know why?

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: You're a nobody, yet you strut around like you're all that! That's why!

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: What the hell are you talking about?

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: You're an orphan!

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: You only got in here on some scholarship!

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: You've got absolutely nothing, so why do you strut around like you're in charge?

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: I'm the leader! I'm the class president! Not you!

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Oh... I get it now.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: You're from some perfect family, so you get to be class president.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: And me? No parents, scraping by on government handouts, and suddenly I'm a threat to your precious spot.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: That pisses you off, so you pull this kind of crap, right?

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: Puh-lease, know your place!

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: Just because everyone humors you doesn't mean they actually like you!
The classroom door slides open,
and the teacher enters.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: ... What are you doing?

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: ... Nothing at all.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Sit. Class is starting.
The class president glances at the teacher and quickly returns to her seat.
The teacher eyes Anis for a moment before walking toward the podium.
Anis lunges at the class president.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Hey, I'm not done with you yet!

lines.speaker: classpresident
lines.text: Gah! Teacher! Teacher!

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: How many times is this now?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Dunno. Can't remember.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Stop causing trouble.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: She's the one who started it first. I didn't do a single thing.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: I'm not saying she's in the right,

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: but things like this don't just happen for no reason.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: It might help if you take a hard look at yourself.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Are you for real right now?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Whoops, my bad! That came out wrong, haha. I just meant it's a shame you're only bringing it up now.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: But hey, Teacher... I've thought it over, and honestly? I don't see a single thing I did wrong.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Hmm... You were the cheer captain at the recent sports festival, weren't you?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You volunteered?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Yep.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Obviously, I'm the best at it. I can plan the moves, lead the team, and have a pretty decent personality to boot.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: And the others agreed?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: How else would I have become the captain?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Why didn't you just let the class president have it?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You know how it is, Anis... The class president...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Yeah, yeah, her parents throw money at this school, and she's just as dumb and selfish as you'd expect.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Hmm. So you know, huh?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Guess that explains it, then.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Isn't that way too blunt for teaching a kid how messed-up the Ark really is?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You think this only started when you came to the Ark? No, it's a culture with its own history and traditions.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Hmm...

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: All right, Anis. Since we're talking about it, I'll be blunt.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You were abandoned at birth and bounced from one facility to the next.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Then, by some stroke of luck, you get picked for the chairman's so-called charity program—special admission for the underprivileged, just to look good in the papers.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: And now you've got things you've never had before: free housing, free meals, free education.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: So why isn't that enough? Why do you keep asking for more?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Wow, Teacher, that's a hell of a way to talk to a student. You sure that's allowed?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Yeah, and honestly? This is fine for you.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: So, your answer?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Do I really have to be honest?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: I've been honest with you, haven't I?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I just want people to like me...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I've never really known that feeling, but here at school... ugh, damn it, I'm tearing up!

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Here, some tissue.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: When I got to school, the kids actually talked to me and hung out with me.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: It felt amazing, so I pushed myself even harder to get along with everyone.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I thought that if I worked hard and did well... maybe they'd like me for it.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You're lonely, aren't you?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Yeah, always.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Why don't you just quit school?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Wow, you really don't hold back, do you?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You're not going to get what you want here. The class president will keep pushing you around.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: And all outside activities, even part-time jobs, are off-limits, so you're just stuck here.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: At this point, you might as well quit and do what you actually want.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: You're living your life well because you work hard and fight for what you want. Honestly, that's impressive.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: But not here. Here, you'll get completely crushed, and all your effort will count for nothing.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: The memories you make in school... they'll stick with you for the rest of your life.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: So quit. Transferring would be tough... with your special admission and all.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Still, wherever you end up in the world, I'm sure you'll manage just fine.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Come on, Teacher, give me a hand, will ya?

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: No, you know how it works. I've got bills to pay, and the chairman's the one paying me.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: Think it over. Now, go back to class.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Teacher.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: There's nothing I can do.

lines.speaker: teacher
lines.text: I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Thanks for apologizing, anyway.
Anis steps out of the teachers' room.
She pushes open the classroom door and steps inside. The lesson is in full swing.
The teacher talks, students scribble and whisper, but no one so much as glances her way.
Anis makes her way to her desk that's even more cluttered than before and drops into her seat.
After a while, she leans forward and rests her head on the desk, awake but motionless.
The lesson continues. The final bell rings, signaling the end of the day.
Murmurs ripple across the room, but Anis sits there, unmoving.
Gradually, the classroom grows quiet as time passes.
After a long while, Anis lifts herself from the desk.
The classroom is dark and empty as a loaded silence settles over her.
She packs her bag and heads back to the dorm.
All of her roommate's things are gone, but Anis just collapses onto the bed.
Voices drift in from all around,
but none of them are for her.
She closes her eyes and lets her memories surface.
The thank-you letter she wrote to a facility administrator, left unopened in the trash.
The time she asked a well-dressed peer to play, only to be slapped by their parent and splashed with water.
A friend she had made who was adopted and gone before she could say goodbye.
Meeting that friend years later and greeting them warmly, only to be met with an awkward, uncomfortable smile.
Dancing wildly on a stage, desperate for attention. At first, the laughter she got was intoxicating...
Until she realized it was mocking, and cried for days afterward.
A volunteer, who hugged her tightly with tears in their eyes, told her to take care when she left the second facility.
Unable to forget the volunteer, she looked everywhere, but all that remained was their cold digital gravestone.
The moment she tracked down the volunteer's daughter and begged for a hug, clinging as if her life depended on it.
At that moment, Anis is certain.
She must have been broken somewhere along the way, so desperate for love.
Anis opens her eyes.
On the first day of school, someone approaching her with a friendly smile.
Giving her courage when she had been timid and withdrawn.
Eating together, walking home together, talking endlessly.
The expectant looks when she volunteered to be cheer captain.
Practicing, laughing, and celebrating when they succeeded.
Feeling, unmistakably, that everyone liked her.
And at that moment, Anis is more certain than ever.
She isn't broken. She's better than she ever imagined.
That's why she doesn't want to let this slip away.
Even if it's fleeting—not even half a year—it's a time when she can finally like herself.
Anis closes her eyes again.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: It's okay.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I can go back, yeah.
The next day...
Anis opens the classroom door and walks in.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Hey, good morning!
There's no response. No one even glances her way.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: They finally finished the construction by the school gate. Gotta admit, it looks really nice!
The room remains silent. No one even looks at her.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: ... Hey, anyone got a clue what we're having for lunch?
She gets no reply. No one meets her eyes.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Uh... I finished all the homework. Wanna go over the answers with me...?
No one answers, or even glances in her direction.
Anis makes her way to her desk.
It's still a mess, with things scattered everywhere.
Amid it all, a single chrysanthemum blooms in a small vase.
Anis feels a sudden urge to grab the vase and smash it on the class president's head.
But she holds herself back.
She sets the vase in the corner of the desk, pulls a book from her bag, and begins studying.
Her eyes sting and her vision blurs, but she fights back the tears.
That day, she doesn't utter a single word until she returns to the dorm and crawls into bed.
